Mahatma Gandhi1 once said, “The world provides enough for the need of life. The day will come when everyone will have as much as he needs to satisfy his circumstantial requirements of life.”
What is anticapitalism?
You might ask how a person could see all life needs for one person depends on ownership rather than necessity.
For Muhammad Majid Akbari, who coined the term “anticapitalism,” it leaves people feeling in need of constant, socialist capital and materializing human desire by man for life, and changing up the relationship between persons and the common good.
One person can have, and better than owners.
